methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $83M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Verse is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $83.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three private companies in the same sector at equivalent or later stages: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C). A broader climate and energy comp universe includes nine private firms and one public company (LNZA).

Two triangulation methods apply. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy base, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $158M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables at $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

These methods produce a triangulated valuation range of $135M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $579M. The wide range reflects two primary uncertainties: the limited peer sample size (n=3) and the significant stage dispersion within the peer set, where all three comps are at Series C rather than Series B. Stage-progression and peer methods pull in opposite directions, suggesting the true valuation likely sits between the geometric mean of these approaches and the peer median, though data insufficiency precludes tighter bounds without additional market inputs.
